correctness.rationale: For fixed d, Looi proves the exact two degree-eigenvalue asymptotics. Their o(1) errors vanish under normalized multiplicity summation; weighted Weyl via Euler integral comparison and Abel summation proves the Fock arcsine limit; a truncated weighted Riemann sum gives all Bergman log-phase limits. The wrapped Exp(d) angular density yields sharp arc extrema, and the Euler-product gamma tail proves the stated d-asymptotics. Boundary zero sets have zero mass, justifying passage to negative-eigenvalue proportions. Numerical checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The antecedent paper arXiv:2603.10879 proves the counterexample symbols, per-degree eigenvalue phases and existence of negative spectral points, but not normalized frequency laws, monomial-multiplicity-weighted empirical measures, exact extrema of negative-mode proportions, or the high-d exponential transition. A relevant published logarithmic spectral-filter result concerns positive smooth radial symbols and logarithmic Dixmier trace asymptotics, not Looi's bounded sign-changing spectrum cutoffs. The new theorem is not a rewording of the known sign of one spectral accumulation point; the complete cutoff distribution needs a separate weighted equidistribution versus phase-dependent Riemann-sum analysis.
residual_risks: Source eigenvalue asymptotics are prior art; remaining novelty lies in averaging/multiplicity/negative-density exact extrema and dimension limit.

value.rationale: The fraction of negative eigenvalues is a natural quantitative index of the severity of failure of essential positivity. The full eigenvalue distribution, weighted by intrinsic monomial multiplicity, is a stronger invariant than existence of negative essential spectrum. The contrasting universal Fock law and extremely intermittent Bergman negative fractions, whose extreme values tend to 0 and 1 with sharp dimension rates, give a motivated exact classification for explicit actively studied counterexamples.
